newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine deputy PM confident of receiving IMF loan.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine deputy PM confident of receiving IMF loan.

text.p: Ukraine's deputy prime minister in charge of reforms said on Thursday he was confident the former Soviet republic would receive a multi-billion dollar credit from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) once it passed its budget.
"We think we can convince them to issue the credit if the budget is passed, which will be in a week to 10 days," Serhiy Tyhypko told reporters at a news conference.

IMF officials said last week the budget was one of 41 conditions Ukraine must meet to receive the three-year, $2.5 to $3 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF), to succeed the $867 million stand-by agreement which expired in February.

Officials from the international funding body have not confirmed Ukrainian media reports of an IMF mission visiting late this month or early next month to review Ukraine's progress toward securing the credit.
The budget, approved at its first reading in December but only returned to parliament after revision by government last week, should have been passed by January 1 under Ukrainian law.
